preconditions.description: The input string is non-empty and has length at most 1000.

preconditions.expression: all(c.islower() or c.isdigit() or c == '.' for c in stdin)
preconditions.description: The input string contains only lowercase letters, digits, and dots.

preconditions.expression: all(len(name) <= 10 and name.isalpha() and name != '' for name in re.findall(r'[a-z]+', stdin))
preconditions.description: Each purchase name is a non-empty string of lowercase letters with length at most 10.

preconditions.expression: all(price != '' and price[0].isdigit() and price[-1].isdigit() and all(c.isdigit() or c == '.' for c in price) for price in re.findall(r'\d+(\.\d+)*', stdin))
preconditions.description: Each price is a non-empty string starting and ending with a digit, containing only digits and dots.

preconditions.expression: all('.' not in price[:-2] or price[-2] == '.' for price in re.findall(r'\d+(\.\d+)*', stdin))
preconditions.description: Dots in prices are either decimal points (with exactly two digits after) or thousand separators (every three digits from the right).

preconditions.expression: all(float(price.replace('.', '')) >= 0.01 and float(price.replace('.', '')) <= 10**6 for price in re.findall(r'\d+(\.\d+)*', stdin))
preconditions.description: Each price is at least one cent and at most 10^6 dollars when parsed as a float.

postconditions.expression: all(c.isdigit() or c == '.' for c in stdout)
postconditions.description: The output string contains only digits and dots.
The output string is non-empty, starts and ends with a digit.

postconditions.expression: all('.' not in stdout[:-2] or stdout[-2] == '.' for c in stdout)
postconditions.description: Dots in the output are either decimal points (with exactly two digits after) or thousand separators (every three digits from the right).

postconditions.expression: float(stdout.replace('.', '')) == sum(float(price.replace('.', '')) for price in re.findall(r'\d+(\.\d+)*', stdin))
postconditions.description: The output represents the sum of all prices in the input, parsed as floats (ignoring thousand separators).

postconditions.expression: not any(stdout.count('.') > 1 and '.' not in stdout[-3:])
postconditions.description: The output does not have consecutive dots unless they are part of a thousand separator or decimal point.
